mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5% mean) in periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts contraction (HOUST < 1.0 million) signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < 1.0 million
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1.0% mean) during episodes where GDPC1 YoY < -2% and HOUST < 1.0 million (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals labor market overheating, which historically precedes Fed tightening and reduced corporate profit margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5% mean) when UNRATE < 4% for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A two-month acceleration in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 0.5% month-over-month indicates robust supply-side expansion, which typically supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5% mean) when INDPRO acceleration exceeds 0.5% for two consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL above 3% and FEDFUNDS above 3.5% for two consecutive months signals a high-inflation, high-rate environment that erodes real earnings and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3% AND FEDFUNDS > 3.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1.0% mean) when CPIAUCSL > 3% and FEDFUNDS > 3.5% for two consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above 5% for three consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and reduced consumer spending, which historically precedes weaker retail sales and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5% mean) when RSAFS > 5% for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 300,000 for two consecutive months combined with a concurrent decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% signals an overheating labor market, which typically triggers restrictive monetary policy and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 300000 for two consecutive months AND UNRATE < 3.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1.0% mean) during episodes of PAYEMS > 300000 for two months and UNRATE < 3.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below -0.3% for four consecutive months signals a broad-based supply contraction, which typically reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5% mean) when INDPRO < -0.3% for four consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).
